title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X is a closed annulus (cylinder) modelled as X = (R/Z) × J, with z = exp(2iπt) and J a symmetric interval in s. The sign operations ε s, εε' s indicate that J is symmetric; the boundary values s = ±1 are inferred from condition (35) and are not stated on this page. The universal cover is X̃ = R × J.

The group G̃ is generated by sign operations (ε, ε') ∈ μ = {±1} × {±1} together with rational affine 'twist' maps f_{a,b}(t,s) = (t + as + b, s), with a, b ∈ Q. It descends to a group G acting on X by (33): (ε,ε').g_{a,θ}(z,s) = ((zθ exp 2iπas)^{ε'}, εε' s), with θ ∈ μ_∞. In this group:
- ε records whether orientation is preserved;
- εε' records whether the two boundary circles are swapped;
- the boundary circles s = ±1 are rotated by θ exp(±2iπa).

The deleted top of this page finishes an abandoned computation from the previous page. It looks for elements with θ exp(±2iπa) = −1, i.e. elements acting as the antipodal rotation on both boundary circles. Writing θ = exp 2iπb, the solutions are a ≡ 1/2, b ≡ 1 or a ≡ 1, b ≡ 1/2 (mod Z).

The retained text restricts to the subgroup G_0 (θ = 1). There g_a(z,s) = (z exp(2iπas), s), and g_a is the identity on ∂X iff exp(±2iπa) = 1, i.e. a ∈ Z. These are the 'straight' twist maps fixing the boundary pointwise. Their isotopy classes rel boundary give the mapping class group of the annulus rel ∂, which is ≅ Z, generated by a Dehn twist.

The next page makes this identification canonical. The generator group is H_1(X) ⊗_{±1} ε_0(X) ≅ Z ⊗_{±1} ω(X): the Dehn-twist generator depends only on an orientation of X, not on a choice of boundary component or of core orientation.

Purpose: in the 'Teichmülleries' project, this sets up the local model for twist parameters along cut curves. It is the annulus piece of the Fenchel–Nielsen / Dehn-twist description of Teichmüller and mapping class groups, and of the action of the extended (orientation-reversing) group, with a rational-twist group G̃ that resembles a 'profinite/rational' enlargement.
errors: No genuine error in the retained text: with J symmetric and boundary at s = ±1, g_a is the identity on ∂X iff a ∈ Z.

Normalization subtlety, not stated on the page: if J = [−1,1], the total twist across the annulus for g_a is 2a. Elements of G_0 fixing ∂X are then even powers of the basic Dehn twist. The single Dehn twist is g_{1/2,θ=−1}, which lies outside G_0, matching the struck solution a ≡ 1/2, b ≡ 1/2 in spirit. Restricting to θ = 1 therefore loses the odd twists, unless J is normalized differently.
The struck (35) reads 'b ≡ 1' with 'a ≡ 1/2' and 'b ≡ 1/2' with 'a ≡ 1'. This is consistent with the previous page's struck solutions (θ = 1, a ∈ 1/2 + Z; θ = −1, a ∈ Z). It was abandoned anyway.

ideas.what: Subgroup of straight twist maps g_a of the annulus fixing the boundary pointwise iff a ∈ Z; these represent the mapping class group of the annulus rel boundary

ideas.what: Extended group with sign data (orientation ε, boundary-component swap εε') and rational twist/rotation parameters (a ∈ Q, θ ∈ μ_∞) acting on the annulus
ideas.modern_name: extended mapping class group of the annulus / rational twists (local model of Fenchel–Nielsen twist coordinates)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine computation: twist maps of an annulus fix the boundary iff the twist parameter is an integer. The more interesting canonical sign bookkeeping, Z ⊗ orientation, is on the next page and is also standard.
transcription_corrections: In (34), the image shows the argument as (z,s) with an overwritten letter and 'exp 2iπ as'. The Θ in 'g_{a,Θ}' and 'Θ = 1' is the θ ∈ μ_∞ of the previous page.
The line 'Pour que cette opération induise l'identité sur ∂X' is correctly read; 'il faut et il suffit qu'on ait' is correct.
The struck system's second line reads 'a ≡ 1, b ≡ 1/2 (Z)'.
